faqs.q: Is NiveshMarg free to start?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sign up, paper trade with virtual money, screen stocks, track a portfolio, use the watchlist and read stock pages on the free Starter plan. Backtesting is part of the Pro plan. AI features run on OpenRouter, and you can add your own OpenRouter key in Settings to choose from 300+ models.

faqs.q: Is paper trading on NiveshMarg real money?
faqs.a: No. Paper trades use virtual money at live market prices. Nothing is sent to a broker and no real money is at risk, which is what makes it a safe way to learn.

faqs.q: Which markets does NiveshMarg cover?
faqs.a: NSE and BSE in India, US exchanges and more than 30 exchanges worldwide. Prices, money and dates are shown in each market's own currency and format.

faqs.q: Does NiveshMarg give investment advice?
faqs.a: No. NiveshMarg is an educational and research tool and is not a SEBI-registered adviser. AI output can be wrong; use it to learn and to organise your research, and consult a registered adviser before investing.

faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
faqs.a: Yes. The NiveshMarg app for Android and iPhone uses the same account as the web dashboard, so your portfolio, watchlist, paper trades and chats are on both.

faqs.q: What is paper trading?
faqs.a: Paper trading is simulated trading: you place buy and sell orders with virtual money at real market prices, and track the profit or loss as if the trade were real — without any real money changing hands.

faqs.q: Are paper trading results the same as real trading?
faqs.a: Not exactly. Simulated trades do not include brokerage, taxes, slippage or liquidity limits, and there is no emotional cost. Treat results as practice, not as a promise of real returns.

faqs.q: Can I short sell in paper trading?
faqs.a: Yes. NiveshMarg paper trading supports both long and short positions so you can practise both directions.

faqs.q: What is backtesting?
faqs.a: Backtesting runs a trading strategy over historical prices to see how it would have performed — its returns, number of trades and worst drawdown — before you use it with real money.

faqs.q: Do I need to code to backtest?
faqs.a: No. Every strategy in the library is ready to run and its settings can be changed from the screen.

faqs.q: Does a good backtest mean the strategy will make money?
faqs.a: No. Past performance does not guarantee future results. A backtest is a first filter; paper trade a strategy going forward before trusting it.

faqs.q: How is the AI Score calculated?
faqs.a: Four readings — forecast, technical, sentiment and trend — are each scored out of 25 and added to a score out of 100. Each reading is shown separately.

faqs.q: Is a high AI Score a buy signal?
faqs.a: No. It is an automated summary of evidence that can be wrong or stale. Use it to learn and to prioritise research, not as advice.
